name: Apapa Port (Lagos)
summary: Nigeria's busiest seaport complex; handles most national container traffic.
description: Apapa and neighbouring Tin Can Island (TCIP) are the Lagos port cluster under the Nigerian Ports Authority, with private terminal operators. Congestion on the Apapa–Oshodi corridor has been a chronic logistics bottleneck. The ports remain the primary import gateway for the southwest and much of the north.
economy: Containers, bulk, tank farms, trucking, bonded terminals.
significance: National import hub, Apapa Wharf, Tin Can Island.

name: Lekki Deep Sea Port
summary: New deep-water port east of Lagos on the Lekki peninsula; 16 m draft container terminal.
description: Lekki Deep Sea Port opened to relieve Lagos congestion with deeper draft and modern quay cranes. It sits within the Lekki Free Zone and connects to the Lekki–Epe expressway. Phase capacity targets multi-million TEU throughput.
economy: Container trade, free zone, logistics parks, real estate.
significance: First greenfield deep-sea port in a generation; Lekki Free Zone anchor.

name: Port Harcourt Port
summary: Oil and general cargo port on the Bonny River up from the Atlantic.
description: Port Harcourt's port (and nearby Onne) serve eastern Nigeria and the oil industry. Draft and dredging limit some vessel classes compared with Lagos; oil-service boats dominate. The city grew around this harbour from 1912.
cargoNote: Oil export support, general cargo, project cargo
economy: Oil export support, general cargo, eastern hinterland.
significance: Garden City harbour, Onne satellite, eastern gateway.

name: Calabar Port
summary: Deep-water port on the Cross River estuary serving the southeast and Cameroon trade.
description: Calabar has been a seaport since the Efik city-state era. The modern port handles general cargo and has been promoted for export processing. Silting and channel maintenance are recurring issues.
cargoNote: General cargo, regional export, EPZ feedstock
economy: General cargo, regional export, limited cruise/tourism.

name: Warri Port
summary: Delta port for oil, steel, and agricultural hinterland cargoes.
description: Warri Port on the Warri River serves the western delta industrial belt including the refinery and steel-related traffic. Access is via dredged delta channels toward Escravos.
cargoNote: Oil products, general cargo, delta hinterland
economy: Oil products, general cargo, delta logistics.

name: Onne Port
summary: Modern deep-water complex east of Port Harcourt; largest Nigerian port by land area.
description: Onne (Federal Ocean Terminal / Federal Lighter Terminal and oil-and-gas free zone) was developed for energy logistics: rigs, pipes, and project cargo. It complements congested Lagos for specialised energy shipments.
economy: Oil services, free zone, project cargo, containers (growing).
significance: Energy logistics hub, free zone, large land take.

name: Western Naval Command (Lagos)
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Western Naval Command; controls the Lagos barrier coast and adjoining maritime area.
description: The Western Naval Command is one of the Nigerian Navy's three principal formations, based in the Lagos area with responsibility for the entire western maritime flank including the Lagos Lagoon, Lekki approaches, and Badagry creeks. It hosts key naval bases, jetties, and security assets for the nation's premier port cluster.
economy: Maritime security, naval base infrastructure, coastal patrol.
significance: Defence of Lagos ports, maritime domain awareness, western coast security.

name: Central Naval Command (Yenagoa / Warri)
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Central Naval Command; responsible for the Niger Delta maritime flank and delta creeks.
description: The Central Naval Command is the Nigerian Navy's delta-facing formation, operating across the Niger Delta creeks from the Escravos/Forcados terminals to Bonny and the central delta waterways. It coordinates JTF maritime components, anti-piracy, and oil-and-gas infrastructure protection.
economy: Delta maritime security, anti-piracy patrols, oil infrastructure defence.
significance: Niger Delta maritime domain and oil-terminal security command.

name: Eastern Naval Command (Calabar)
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Eastern Naval Command; covers the Cross River estuary, eastern seaboard, and Cameroon border maritime approaches.
description: The Eastern Naval Command is the Nigerian Navy's formation for the eastern coast, including the Cross River estuary at Calabar, Akwa Ibom coast, and the Bakassi/Cameroon maritime frontier. It supports Calabar Port security and joint border maritime operations.
economy: Eastern seaboard maritime security, Calabar port defence, Cameroon border patrol.
significance: Defence of the eastern coast, Cross River estuary, and Calabar harbour.
